fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Dylan Saccoccio joins Chance for their first one-on-one conversation, building on Dylan's Spirit Whirled book series, research into the natural laws encoded inside language, etymology, and symbolism that most people absorb unconsciously their entire lives.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In this session: the 2020 election as political theater and why the outcome never changes the underlying system, universal basic income and why a digital currency with expiration dates is pure control, Dylan's years inside Hollywood and finance and why he walked away, the 10,000 hours concept as a mechanism of indoctrination, flattery as the first tool of the psychic vampire, the real astronomical meaning of Satan as adversary, and the first three of the four tenets of satanism, ego, moral relativism, and social darwinism. The fourth is in the extended episode.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Tenets Completed", "body": "Dylan finishes the four tenets of Satanism he opened in the free hour. He reads Luke 11:21 through 22 from the King James Bible and calls the passage Abrahamic Luciferian Satanism, social Darwinism encoded in scripture, then names the final tenet, eugenics, which he ties to the divine right of kings and describes as tinkering with the natural world to suit the well-born. Chance answers with his own reading of the parable as a warning about abandoning natural law, decoding grocery and usury along the way. Dylan closes by sending listeners to Mark Passio's first 160 or so podcasts."}, {"title": "The Two Languages", "body": "Chance raises the old split between hieratic and demotic scripts and argues the modern version is legalese, a language he describes as copyrighted and owned by the Crown Corporation, where even the word separate means several. He follows a thread in which the divine name was pulled from the King James Bible and replaced with Lord, a title he links to Baal. Dylan, reluctant to wade into religious controversy, still offers his reading that YHWH is pronounced Hova, that the Book of Job should be the Book of Jove, and that the Pope's own pronunciation confirms it."}, {"title": "Word Magic and Its Techniques", "body": "Dylan names homonyms as one of the priest class techniques his books teach, right after Chance plays idol against idle and calls idolatry idleness, a comparison he credits to Clint Richardson. Dylan adds that fetishism was the older word for idolatry and marks the end stage of a collapsing religion that has lost the spiritual meaning of its symbols. Chance's summary claim is that sorcery requires people to believe symbols are what they represent, and his antidote is remembering you are not a person, place, or thing, since nouns are abstractions and reality keeps becoming."}, {"title": "The Digital Enclosure", "body": "Dylan's warning about cryptocurrency is that a currency which is conceptual rather than actual can be censored the way social media already censors speech, offers no generational store of value, and leads toward a locked-down economy. Chance tells his story of a new work computer that Microsoft would not let anyone use without an online account, a preview of owning nothing, and throws in his epiphany that rent also means torn asunder. Dylan advises moving wealth into tangible things held in allodium, with nobody above you, and warns that blockchain ledgers could track every aspect of life inside a legal digital farm."}, {"title": "Collapse and Regeneration", "body": "A late stretch turns Dylan's story of being moved to tears by Red Dead Redemption 2 into Chance's realization that charity and giving for their own sake are how a person becomes regenerate, aligned with a nature that keeps rebirthing itself like a phoenix. Dylan holds that most people will not look into what is going on until they have lost everything, the way junkies have to hit rock bottom. Dylan urges calm and a good foundation of mind as systems collapse, while Chance argues the only way to lead anyone out of Babylon is to get healthy and carry equipoise, the balance Dylan calls magic in his fantasy series."}]
